projects.name: IkanAdapt
projects.fullName: IkanAdapt — Enabling fisheries and aquaculture stakeholders in Timor-Leste to adapt to climate change, increase resilience and conserve biodiversity
projects.summary: Helps fishing and fish-farming communities in Timor-Leste adapt to climate change and build resilience using nature-based solutions that also protect biodiversity.
projects.description:
Timor-Leste faces significant challenges in addressing climate change impacts, protecting biodiversity and sustainably managing its aquatic and coastal resources. Contributing factors include weak governance, limited organizational and technical capacity and knowledge, and limited resources for developing and implementing adaptation and biodiversity plans.

IkanAdapt aims to support fishery- and aquaculture-dependent communities to become more resilient to climate variability and change, using nature-based solutions that benefit both communities and biodiversity. It directly addresses five of the seven priorities in the National Adaptation Plan: risk management capacity-building, addressing the needs of vulnerable communities, ecosystem-based coastal disaster risk reduction, sustainable land management, and climate-resilient livelihoods.

The project builds on existing government and partner programmes and emerging good practice, applying the Ecosystem Approach to Fisheries and Aquaculture (EAF/EAA) and Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA) following the principles of Nature-based Solutions. Implementation is led by WorldFish in close collaboration with the Timor-Leste Directorate for Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Resources Management and FAO.

It works through three outcome areas:
1. Enabling national fisheries and aquaculture policies, programmes, legal frameworks and local management institutions to address climate change, current variability and biodiversity conservation.
2. Enhancing climate change adaptation and biodiversity conservation capacity and practices in fishing and fish-farming communities (coastal and inland).
3. Strengthening institutional capacity through climate- and biodiversity-related information systems, information management and monitoring operations.

projects.name: Peskas
projects.fullName: Peskas — open-source digital platform for small-scale fisheries
projects.summary: An open-source platform that turns what small-scale fishers land and where they go into validated catch, effort and revenue data that fisheries agencies can act on.
projects.description:
Peskas is modular rather than monolithic: per-country data pipelines ingest landing surveys (KoboToolbox) and boat GPS tracks (Pelagic Data Systems), process them through a shared R library, and publish validated data to national dashboards, a regional portal, an API and a fisher-facing app.

The design point is reuse. A country joining the platform does not get a bespoke build — it gets the shared pipeline and portal configured for its fleet, its surveys and its authority. That is why the marginal cost of the next country is lower than the last.

Started in Timor-Leste and now running with national fisheries institutions in Kenya, Zanzibar, Mozambique and Malawi, with Malaysia in preparation.
partners: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Forestry (Timor-Leste)
Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute (KEFS)
DINAPA — National Directorate of Fisheries and Aquaculture (Mozambique)

projects.name: FASA
projects.fullName: Development and Scaling of Sustainable Feeds for Resilient Aquatic Food Systems in Sub-Saharan Africa
projects.summary: Making better fish feed decisions possible for smallholder farmers in sub-Saharan Africa, where imported feed is the largest cost and the biggest constraint on growth.
projects.description:
Feed is typically the dominant cost in smallholder aquaculture, and formulating it well requires nutrition data and optimisation expertise that farmers and local feed producers rarely have access to.

FASA assembles the reference data needed to answer the question — species nutrient requirements, ingredient composition, and worked formulations — and puts a least-cost formulation tool on top of it, so a decision that normally needs a feed nutritionist can be made locally with locally available ingredients.
